rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L60 maintainer block: "re-audit @796293b 2026-05-31: writing PASS, pedagogy PASS — steer-callout gained a premature-completion recovery line (§48/§62) + a render-as-HTML affordance callout after the shapes prompt (§50/§53/§62 hold)". Verb 'gained' narrates a completed transition (the callout GAINED a feature over time), which is exactly the tense-test tell this rule bans in a maintainer block: 'restored after a judge caught it', 'was softened' are the licensed examples of what to cut, and 'gained a ... line ... after the shapes prompt' is the same shape. This differs from the L52/L56 dated provenance headers directly above it, which the rule explicitly carves out because they anchor a still-binding constraint (bullet-emphasis budget, lean-pass cut list) rather than narrate a diff. The harm: a reader who never saw the pre-2026-05-31 version of this file loses nothing actionable if this clause is deleted — the live body already has whatever the recovery line and HTML-affordance callout now say. No accept-note in the maintainer block specifically licenses this row's wording.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rewrite as present-tense state (what the steer-callout currently does) or drop the row — the 'judges @289b45a3' line above it already carries the current per-class ledger, and if the finding is worth preserving it belongs in git history, not a second changelog line in the maintainer block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all four sub-shapes: (a) empty negation — L7 'no fork' is a real distinguishing instruction (worktree vs. a git fork), not a rhetorical negation against a misconception no reader would hold; (b) deictic drumroll ('That is the X') — none present; (c) bold-label echo (`**Label.** Label restated...`) — the structural leads (**What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:**, **Time:**) are canonical module-shape fields, not content-echoing labels, and none is restated as the following sentence's grammatical subject; (d) citation/appendix duplication — the only source citation lives in the backing block, not duplicated inline in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L30 'a ranked gap list of three to five items' specifies a target range for an artifact the reader has not yet produced (no adjacent bulleted list of gap items exists in body for this count to duplicate) — it is a spec for the output, not a stale tally of visible bullets. No section header carries a redundant count either.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L13 "The point: two sessions are enough to place every lesson." 'every' is the superlative tell. Read narrowly ('place' = categorize/route each observed gap to memory/verifier/skill, per P1's own 'Where the fix belongs' dimension, scoped to this exercise's own two artifacts — the 'artifact we built' carve-out), the claim holds. Read broadly (two sessions surface literally every lesson available about agentic development), a professional reader finds a counterexample immediately, and the file's own maintainer failure-modes ('Packaging over-credit', 'Rule-cut dodge') implicitly concede the diagnosis does not automatically place every lesson — only that a rigorous student CAN get there. The backing block's Stance ledger already frames this as a deliberate house position with a stated would-move-it condition, so this reads as a genuine open rule question rather than a clear defect: is 'every lesson' meant to be scoped to what this exercise's own two runs are built to surface, or as a general epistemic claim the file's own fallback undercuts?
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either scope the line explicitly ('two sessions are enough to place what this exercise is built to catch') or leave it as is if the maintainer confirms the narrow reading is the intended one — do not hedge it into mush either way.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: L34-35, 'Two sessions of the same task were the first real stress-test of `./CLAUDE.local.md`. Diagnosis surfaced rules that turned out wrong, never fired when they should have, or fired and made the session worse.' then 'Rules-files have a half-life. Adding rules is only half of it; subtracting the dead ones is the other half.' — two bullets, two distinct claims (this instance was a stress-test vs. the general half-life principle), not a three-sentence restatement of one idea at different altitudes; no §21-owned sentence sitting under a third recap.

The one pre-prompt decision point (L7, deciding whether the M5 session is 'done enough') is a plausibly-failable, student-owned judgement call about their own in-progress work, not an unfounded gate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L30 'Close with a ranked gap list of three to five items and a dominant gap.' names no actor. Read in context (end of a push-back coaching section, and P2's own fence later refers to 'the gap list I just ranked' as something already in scrollback), this most likely describes the conversational exchange's outcome — Claude produces the ranked list through the push-back loop — not a demand that the student personally compile it by hand. But the sentence itself does not say 'ask Claude to close with...', and the rule's own diagnostic is explicit that an actor-unnamed sentence defaults to manual by design ('vagueness is not neutral here; it defaults to manual'). Low-confidence: everywhere else in this section the actor is Claude (L28 'Claude will likely open...', L29 'If Claude writes...'), which supports reading L30 the same way, but the sentence doesn't say so on its own.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If the intent is that Claude's response (after push-back) closes with the ranked list, make that explicit — e.g. 'Push Claude until its answer closes with a ranked gap list of three to five items and a dominant gap.'

This is a narrow, genuinely debatable register call, not a clear-cut miss — L22/L29/L37 (plain 'Ask Claude to...' invocations) are unambiguously correct as-is.
